summary:
**ASTRAJECT – Design the Mission. Engineer the Future.**

ASTRAJECT is an interactive, browser-based space mission design and simulation game developed by Team ASTRAVYN for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It allows students and space enthusiasts to experience the role of a spacecraft mission engineer by designing, launching, and operating their own space missions.

Through an 8-step Mission Designer, users select spacecraft components, instruments, power systems, communication systems, orbits, and launch vehicles. The platform provides live engineering calculations and validation across six resource areas: mass, power, budget, data, communications, and mission time. Players can then launch missions, monitor 3D orbital visualizations and real-time telemetry, encounter simulated spacecraft anomalies, and observe automatic recovery. A final scoring system evaluates mission performance and provides feedback for improvement.

ASTRAJECT addresses the challenge by transforming complex aerospace concepts into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. It encourages systems thinking, experimentation, problem-solving, and learning through safe failure.
details:
Project Details – ASTRAJECT | Team ASTRAVYN

ASTRAJECT is an interactive, browser-based space mission design and simulation game that transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into a hands-on learning experience. It allows users to act as spacecraft mission engineers, making decisions that directly influence mission performance.

How it works: Users choose from Earth, Moon, and Mars mission campaigns or create a custom mission in Sandbox mode. Through an 8-step Mission Designer, they select spacecraft components, scientific instruments, power systems, communication systems, orbital parameters, and launch vehicles. The platform continuously calculates and validates six essential resource areas: mass, power, budget, data, communications, and mission time. Once the design passes its readiness checks, users launch the spacecraft and enter Mission Control, where they monitor 3D orbital visualization, live telemetry, battery levels, science-data collection, and communication performance. Simulated spacecraft anomalies introduce operational challenges, with automatic recovery mechanisms. At mission completion, a transparent scoring system evaluates performance and provides feedback through mission reports.

Benefits and intended impact: ASTRAJECT makes aerospace engineering more accessible to high-school students, university learners, educators, and space enthusiasts. Instead of learning scientific concepts separately, users understand how spacecraft systems interact. They can experiment safely, experience simulated failures, understand engineering trade-offs, and improve their designs through repeated missions. The intended impact is to encourage STEM education, scientific curiosity, systems thinking, and interest in future space exploration.

Technology used: The project was developed using JavaScript and React 19, with Vite for development and building, Tailwind CSS for interface styling, Three.js for 3D visualization, Recharts for telemetry graphs, Framer Motion for animations, and Lucide for icons. React Context API manages application state, Vitest supports automated testing, and browser LocalStorage provides local mission persistence. The application is designed to run in a web browser without requiring specialized physical hardware or a dedicated desktop installation.

Creativity and innovation: ASTRAJECT connects the complete space mission lifecycle—from spacecraft design and engineering calculations to launch, real-time operations, unexpected anomalies, recovery, and final evaluation—in one interactive experience. Its unique educational approach is to make every engineering decision produce visible consequences.

Factors considered: Our team considered scientific plausibility, educational accessibility, interconnected resource constraints, different difficulty levels, mission destinations, user experience, simulation reliability, and the balance between realistic engineering concepts and understandable gameplay. We use simplified physics models for education and clearly distinguish the simulation from professional spacecraft design tools.

ASTRAJECT's vision is to inspire learners to think, experiment, solve problems, and understand the engineering challenges behind space exploration.
